sources: Platner-Ashby s.v. Via Appia (read): flanked with tombs; Via Latina (read): the triangle between the two roads occupied by tombs

regiones_augustae.text: An irregular strip from the east corner of the Palatine south past the Porta Capena, bounded on the west by the Palatine and never more than about 150 m wide on average; beyond the Aventine it widened to the Almo, outside the Aurelian wall.

sources: Platner-Ashby s.v. Regiones Quattuordecim (read)
regiones_augustae.text: Most of the Caelian, bounded by Region I, the Aurelian wall, and the straight street from the Colosseum to the Porta Caelimontana and Porta Asinaria.

sources: Platner-Ashby s.v. Regiones Quattuordecim (read)
regiones_augustae.text: The Colosseum valley and the Oppius, bounded by Region II, the Servian wall, the Clivus Suburanus from the Porta Esquilina west and its prolongation to a point north of the Colosseum, then south to the Meta Sudans. The name comes from temples of Isis and Serapis later built there.

sources: Platner-Ashby s.v. Regiones Quattuordecim (read)
regiones_augustae.text: The Sacra via from its beginning to the atrium Vestae, the Subura and the Cispius; bounded by Region III's line, the Servian wall, the vicus Patricius from the Porta Viminalis to near the Subura, and the line between the Fora of Nerva and Vespasian, embracing the northern part of the Forum. (The name Templum Pacis dates from Vespasian.)

sources: Platner-Ashby s.v. Regiones Quattuordecim (read)
regiones_augustae.text: The eastern district outside the Servian wall, north of the via Asinaria. In Augustus' time the Campus Viminalis and the ground between the via Tiburtina and the via Salaria lay outside the city and were not in Region V until after Vespasian; the boundary was 300-400 m beyond the later Aurelian wall on the south.

sources: Platner-Ashby s.v. Regiones Quattuordecim (read)
Platner-Ashby s.v. Alta Semita (read)
regiones_augustae.text: The Quirinal from the imperial fora to the Servian wall between the Porta Viminalis and the Porta Collina, west far enough to take in the horti Sallustiani and north beyond the later Aurelian wall; named for the Alta Semita along the ridge.

sources: Platner-Ashby s.v. Regiones Quattuordecim (read)
regiones_augustae.text: Named for the southern end of the Via Flaminia (the Corso); lay between the Via Flaminia and the western boundary of Region VI, i.e. the east side of the Corso up the slope of the Pincian.

sources: Platner-Ashby s.v. Regiones Quattuordecim (read)
regiones_augustae.text: An irregular region: the Forum (not the whole Sacra via), the (later) imperial fora, the Capitol and the ground south of it, extending to a line drawn north of the Forum Boarium through the Velabrum to the east end of the atrium Vestae.

sources: Platner-Ashby s.v. Regiones Quattuordecim (read)
Platner-Ashby s.v. Campus Martius (read)
regiones_augustae.text: All the ground between the Servian wall, the Via Flaminia and the Tiber: the Campus Martius. After Augustus the name Campus Martius was restricted to the part west of the Via Lata; a boundary stone found near the Pantheon shows that in Augustus' time the southern part was more or less built over and the northern part was open meadow.

sources: Platner-Ashby s.v. Regiones Quattuordecim (read)
Tac. Ann. 12.24
regiones_augustae.text: The Palatine within the lines Tacitus gives for the first pomerium.

sources: Platner-Ashby s.v. Regiones Quattuordecim (read)
regiones_augustae.text: A very irregular region containing the Circus Maximus and the Forum Boarium, bounded by the Tiber and Regions IX, VIII, X, XII and XIII.

sources: Platner-Ashby s.v. Regiones Quattuordecim (read)
regiones_augustae.text: The eastern part of the Aventine and the ground toward the Via Appia; named for a former public reservoir. Bounded by the Via Appia and Region I, the Aurelian wall, and the vicus portae Raudusculanae and vicus Piscinae Publicae.

sources: Platner-Ashby s.v. Regiones Quattuordecim (read)
regiones_augustae.text: The Aventine and the district south of it, between the boundaries of Region XII and XI, the Aurelian wall, and the Tiber.

sources: Platner-Ashby s.v. Regiones Quattuordecim (read)
regiones_augustae.text: All the city on the right bank of the Tiber (Trastevere), with the Tiber island; its limits cannot be fixed, but it included much more than the area within the Aurelian wall: south to the temple of Fors Fortuna, north to include the Vatican district.

sources: Platner-Ashby s.v. Regiones Quattuor (read)
Varro LL 5.45-54
regiones_servianae.text: Comprised the Sucusa (Caelian spur), the Ceroliensis (the saddle between the Palatine and the Esquiline, with the Carinae) and the Caelius, by the generally accepted view, which is sharply disputed.

sources: Platner-Ashby s.v. Regiones Quattuor (read)
regiones_servianae.text: The Oppius and Cispius spurs of the Esquiline.

sources: Platner-Ashby s.v. Regiones Quattuor (read)
Platner-Ashby s.v. Regiones Quattuor (read)
Varro LL 5.45-54
regiones_servianae.text: The Palatium, the Velia and the Cermalus (Germalus). All the area inside the pomerium belonged to the four regions except, apparently, the Capitoline, which was the citadel and religious centre; the Aventine lay outside the pomerium. The division stayed in force until Augustus' reorganisation.
